kernel_family: gemm_basic (TileLang fe6d319c, sm_121a, TMA + producer warp group)

launch_us.source: ablation kt0_nostore, 1 block, CUDA-event median: launch + one block's setup + event overhead

block_setup_us.source: ablation kt0_nostore, 1 block, %globaltimer span inside the block: descriptor prefetch, barrier init, register reconfig

block_launch_rate_us_per_block.source: ablation kt0_nostore, full grid minus 1 block over blocks, at 8192^3 (2048 blocks): the block scheduler's issue rate when blocks are empty

store_us_per_KB_per_block.source: ablation kt0 minus kt0_nostore, 1 block, %globaltimer: the fragment-to-global store of one C tile, per KB of tile

tensor_rate_TFs_per_SM.source: ablation noload, 1 block: (block span - setup) / KT over the k-tile's FLOPs; per tile in blocks[]
tensor_rate_TFs_per_SM.note: per-pick values 2.16-2.70; B31 measured 2.52 with a full-occupancy mma loop

load_rate_alone_GBs_per_block.source: ablation nocompute, 1 block: one block's TMA pipeline alone, bytes per k-tile over (span - setup)/KT; 77-87 GB/s on every pick
load_rate_alone_GBs_per_block.note: B8 measured 31 GB/s per SM for a single resident 16 KB tile; the pipelined kernel reaches 2.5x that

load_rate_chip_GBs.source: ablation nocompute at 48 / 96 / full grid: grid bytes over kernel span; the L2-resident shapes reach 1.2-1.7 TB/s, the DRAM-bound ones (8192^3) 0.85 TB/s of L2 traffic over 211 GB/s of DRAM

dram_rate_GBs.source: ablation full kernel at M=32 (B streamed once, 33.5 MB, warm L2, CUDA events): the rate the TMA pipeline reaches from DRAM

sync_per_ktile_us.source: ablation full minus max(compute alone, loads under the full grid) per block, over KT: what the mbarrier hand-off costs per k-tile when the pipeline overlaps

wave_quantisation.source: TileLang compiles of the 1024^3 pick's tile at one row of 47..97 tiles, do_bench timing (includes the do_bench offset below)
wave_quantisation.note: no step at 49 or 97: the scheduler refills SMs as blocks finish; time grows with blocks/48 smoothly, ceil() is wrong

panel_traffic_4096.source: ncu on the 4096^3 pick with its panel (16) and with panel 0: lookup-miss sectors x 32 B

do_bench_offset_us.source: host_overhead.py on the 1024^3 pick: TileLang do_bench event median 73.6 us against 47.8 us wall-clock per call back-to-back and 45.1 us in the ablation harness; cuTensorMapEncodeTiled is 0.47 us
do_bench_offset_us.note: every sweep, sample and baseline timing taken through do_bench carries this per-call offset; the harness and cuBLASLt's harness do not
do_bench_offset_us.mechanism: tilelang/profiler/bench.py: do_bench writes a 256 MB flush buffer between timed calls (fast_flush, cache_size=256). The timed kernel then starts with a cold L2 (A and B come from DRAM: 6.3 MB / 235 GB/s = 27 us at 1024^3) and with dirty lines draining to DRAM (up to 24 MB). The offset is per call, not per launch, and it is largest where the kernel is short or DRAM-bound. The ablation harness and the cuBLASLt harness time back-to-back launches with a warm L2; the two conditions are both real, and they must not be mixed.
